`final class RenderState`<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.lib.bridge.render.state` · **Module:** `core` · **Source:** [RenderState.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/core/src/main/java/dev/joid/lib/bridge/render/state/RenderState.java)

The settings that every draw reads, color, blending, texture, shader, lines, depth, stencil, viewport and target.

## Description

`getState()` of the render bridge, `BridgeHandler.RENDER.get()`, holds the current state.
Change it inside `withState(...)` of the render bridge, which restores it afterwards, even when your code throws; the setters return the state, so they chain.

| [textureMipmap](#RenderState-property-textureMipmap) | `boolean` | `true` | If `false`, the next draws sample the texture without its mip levels, even when it has some. |

| [textureFilter](#RenderState-property-textureFilter) | [`TextureFilter`](/reference/bridges/texturefilter/) | `TextureFilter.NEAREST` | How the texture is sampled between its pixels, a [`TextureFilter`](/reference/bridges/texturefilter/). |
| [colorWrite](#RenderState-property-colorWrite) | `boolean` | `true` | If `false`, the draws write nothing into the color channels, only depth or stencil, as the masks do. |

<a id="RenderState-property-cull"></a>

### cull

- `this cull(boolean cull)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

<a id="RenderState-property-lighting"></a>

### lighting

- `this lighting(boolean lighting)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `boolean isLighting()` 

**Default:** `false`

If `true`, the default shader shades each vertex by its normal, with a light that faces the viewer, as for 3D models.

<a id="RenderState-property-lineWidth"></a>

### lineWidth

- `this lineWidth(float lineWidth)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `float getLineWidth()` 

**Default:** `1F`

Width of the lines that the [`Tessellator`](/reference/drawing/tessellator/) draws, in screen pixels.
A width other than `1F` draws each segment as a quad.

<a id="RenderState-property-depthTest"></a>

### depthTest

- `this depthTest(boolean depthTest)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `boolean isDepthTest()` 

**Default:** `false`

If `true`, a fragment farther than the depth already stored is discarded.

<a id="RenderState-property-depthWrite"></a>

### depthWrite

- `this depthWrite(boolean depthWrite)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `boolean isDepthWrite()` 

**Default:** `true`

<a id="RenderState-property-lineSmooth"></a>

### lineSmooth

- `this lineSmooth(boolean lineSmooth)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `boolean isLineSmooth()` 

**Default:** `false`

If `true`, the lines get antialiased edges.

<a id="RenderState-property-alphaCutoff"></a>

### alphaCutoff

- `this alphaCutoff(float alphaCutoff)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `float getAlphaCutoff()` 

**Default:** `0F`

Alpha, on 1, at or below which the shaders discard a fragment; `0F` keeps every fragment.
[`UI.mask`](/reference/ui/ui/#UI-method-mask) sets `0.5F` to keep only the opaque part of an image.

- `BlendState getBlend()` 

**Default:** `BlendState.DISABLED`

How the next draws combine with the pixels already on the target, a [`BlendState`](/reference/pipeline/blendstate/).

<a id="RenderState-property-stencil"></a>

### stencil

- `this stencil(StencilState stencil)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `StencilState getStencil()` 

**Default:** `StencilState.DISABLED`

Stencil test and operations of the next draws, a [`StencilState`](/reference/pipeline/stencilstate/).
It works on the window only: a framebuffer has no stencil.

<a id="RenderState-property-shader"></a>

### shader

- `this shader(IShader shader)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `IShader getShader()` 

**Default:** `null`

Shader of the next draws; `null` draws with the default shader of the backend, which draws the vertex colors and the texture.
A [`ShaderProgram`](/reference/shaders/shaderprogram/) sets it while it is bound.

<a id="RenderState-property-texture"></a>

- `this texture(ITexture texture)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `ITexture getTexture()` 

**Default:** `null`

Texture that the next draws sample; `null` draws plain colors.
Setting a texture turns `textureMipmap` back on.

## Method details

<a id="RenderState-method-color"></a>

### color

`this color(float red, float green, float blue, float alpha)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Sets the current color, channels on 1: the color of the vertices that carry none, so it tints a textured draw without vertex colors.

<a id="RenderState-method-viewport"></a>

### viewport

`this viewport(int x, int y, int width, int height)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Sets the rectangle of the target that the projection maps to, in pixels: `x`, `y` from the bottom-left corner, `width`, `height`.
A draw with an empty viewport draws nothing.
